practices.practice: Reuse a single long-lived MongoClient (share the driver instance/pool) for the process and do not create a new client per request.

practices.practice: Do not hard-code the cluster connection string or credentials in source; read DOCUMENTDB_URI (or MONGODB_URI) from environment/config and keep secrets out of the repo (use Key Vault or other secret store).
practices.prior_belief: Never hard‑code the DocumentDB/Cosmos connection string or credentials in source. Read DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment at runtime and prefer storing secrets in Azure Key Vault; do not write the secret into logs, files or test fixtures.

practices.practice: Enforce TLS for client connections and restrict network access with cluster firewall rules or Private Link; prefer private endpoints for production instead of exposing the public endpoint.
practices.prior_belief: Use TLS/SSL for the MongoDB connection (ensure the client enforces certificate validation) and restrict network access to the cluster via IP firewall rules or VNet/Private Endpoint; do not expose DB to the public internet without allowlisting.

practices.practice: When sharding a collection, choose a high-cardinality, immutable shard key that aligns with common query patterns so most requests are routed to a single shard.
practices.prior_belief: Choose a high‑cardinality, immutable partition/shard key at collection creation (for example: tenant_id or customer_id) to avoid cross‑partition queries; design all heavy lookups and writes to include the partition key.

practices.practice: Provision throughput thoughtfully and use autoscale tiers where appropriate, and monitor provisioned vs consumed throughput (RU/s) so ingestion, vector indexing and enrichment don't throttle other workloads.
practices.prior_belief: Provision throughput thoughtfully: use autoscale or set collection RU/s so ingestion, vector search and enrich steps do not throttle other workloads; monitor RU consumption and set alerts.

practices.practice: Create indexes that match your query patterns: index every field used in filters or sorts and create compound indexes for common multi-field predicates to avoid COLLSCANs.
practices.prior_belief: Index every field used in filters, sorts, or join/lookup stages (e.g., normalized_email, phone_normalized, tenant_id, workflow_run_id). Create compound indexes for common multi‑field predicates (e.g., {tenant_id:1, normalized_email:1}).

practices.practice: Use a TTL index (expireAfterSeconds on _ts or a custom TTL field) to automatically expire transient workflow or log documents so collections don't grow indefinitely.
practices.prior_belief: Create a TTL policy for transient workflow/log documents (use a date field + expireAfterSeconds TTL index or the provider TTL feature) so orchestrator run documents auto‑expire and do not grow indefinitely.

practices.practice: Avoid large offset/skip pagination for large datasets; implement keyset (range/continuation token) pagination by sorting on an indexed, unique field and using a last-seen cursor.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid using skip/offset for large pagination; implement range (cursor) pagination by sorting on an indexed field (e.g., created_at or _id) and using a last_seen value to page efficiently.

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB supports multi-document ACID transactions (use startSession()/withTransaction in drivers) including cross-collection and cross-shard transactions where supported; use driver sessions and transaction APIs to group operations when atomicity across documents is required.
practices.prior_belief: For dedupe/merge operations, prefer single‑document atomic updates or use findAndModify / find_one_and_update patterns that return the post‑update document rather than multi‑document cross‑partition transactions; design data to minimize cross‑partition transactions.
practices.source_name: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff and jitter for transient network errors and throttling (429/RequestRateTooLarge) and honor Retry-After/retry-after-ms headers when provided; prefer enqueuing/retrying background work instead of blocking threads.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retries with exponential backoff and jitter for transient network or server errors (e.g., network timeouts, 429/RequestRateTooLarge); detect throttling responses and back off according to Retry‑After where provided.
practices.source_name: Design throttling to improve resilience

practices.prior_belief: Enable and use query explain plans and index usage statistics to verify that dedupe and ingest queries are using the intended indexes; check queryPlanner/explain for slow aggregation pipelines.

practices.practice: Store vector embeddings as first-class numeric arrays alongside documents and create a dedicated vector index (cosmosSearch) — Azure DocumentDB provides an integrated vector store so you can keep embeddings with the document rather than requiring an external vector DB.
practices.prior_belief: Model customer profiles to embed small, frequently‑accessed subdocuments (addresses, contact points) and reference or store large vectors/attachments in separate collections to avoid document size limits and to keep hot documents small.

practices.practice: Store embeddings as a number[] and index them with a dedicated vector index (specify dimensions and similarity metric), because vectors that are not numeric arrays are not indexed and won't be returned by vector search.
practices.prior_belief: Store vector embeddings as a dense numeric array of floats and keep dimension metadata. Create a dedicated vector index on the embedding field (specifying dimension and metric like cosine/L2) rather than attempting to search raw arrays with standard indexes.

practices.prior_belief: When a managed vector index/engine is provided (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF), create the vector index through the provider API/tooling (MCP/portal or createIndexes with vectorOptions) and include parameters: field path, dims, index type and metric; do not rely on emulating vector search with regular queries.
